failures.criterion: The architect's rule for a live claim whose plugin is below the update contract: it cannot answer an update task, so when it is not in a turn the daemon relaunches it in its own session onto the pinned plugin pair, in the same pod with its disk kept, and a claim in a turn is relaunched once that turn ends. Decided from the live case of 2026-10-30: after the 16:59Z boot on the newer contract, INFRA-825's claims came up on the previous image at plugin contract 42, every legion tool call failed, and the daemon went on routing work to them until an operator moved the issue by hand at 18:03Z.
failures.evidence:
RED TEST: packages/daemon/internal/supervise/stale_contract_test.go, TestAStalePluginBelowTheUpdateContractIsRelaunchedWhenItsTurnEnds, committed on legion/INFRA-484. Command: `cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/supervise -run TestAStalePluginBelowTheUpdateContractIsRelaunchedWhenItsTurnEnds -count=1 -v`. Its first row PASSES and its second FAILS at 7fa2fb2265e5.

Half the rule already holds. A claim at contract 42 that is idle is relaunched at once: state launching, one Resume over the recorded process at generation 2 resuming the claim's own session file, PluginRelaunchFor set to this daemon's contract, no round opened and no prompt sent (refreshPlugin reaches relaunchStale through CannotAnswerUpdate, plugin.go:104-107). The relaunch is a Resume of the recorded process, which under the Kubernetes runtime keeps the pod and its disk.

The other half does not. A claim at contract 42 that is in a turn is relaunched where it stands: observed `state=launching` immediately after the StalePlugin post, one Resume already made, and the pending task taken back marked `interrupted=true`. The code says so itself — relaunchStale calls replaceProcess with the reason 'the process on another plugin contract is replaced mid-turn' (plugin.go:124), and refreshPlugin's own comment states the cost: 'relaunchStale ends the turn in flight, and a worker that never pushed loses that turn's work with it'. That is the harm this issue exists to end, and it falls on exactly the worker that cannot be asked to push first, since it has no ready_for_update op. The wait costs nothing: such a claim holds no round open, nothing else of its pod waits on it, and the machine already waits a turn out this way for a held suspension and for a plugin round's own end (TestPodUpdateEndedInAPluginRoundRelaunchesOnceTheTurnIsOver).

One existing test pins the rule being changed and is the implementer's to change with the fix: packages/daemon/internal/supervise/plugin_test.go:72, TestAStalePluginMidTurnInterruptsTheTaskChargingNothing. Its harness registers at contract 24, below PodUpdateContract, so it takes the same relaunchStale path and asserts the interruption this rule replaces.
